pr_title: Configure Http.sys UrlGroup when CreateOrAttach is specified and the specified UrlPrefixes do not exist
pr_body:
This change ensures any specified UrlPrefixes are properly configured when RequestQueueMode.CreateOrAttach is specified and the queue already exists. Before this change, if the queue exists, any specified prefixes are ignored and we assumed the process which created the queue already set up the prefixes. This may not always be the case (e.g. in the queue delegation scenario) so this change always tries to register the specified prefixes but ignores errors if the prefix was already setup for the queue. 

As part of this change, I also reversed the relationship between UrlGroup and RequestQueue. Previously RequestQueue had a reference to UrlGroup. I changed it so that UrlGroup references a RequestQueue. This makes more sense with how http.sys works (multiple UrlGroups can be linked to a RequestQueue but a UrlGroup can only be linked to one RequestQueue). This also made the code with my changes cleaner. 

Fixes #40359

issue_context.title: Http.sys server should support setting up URL groups when attaching to an existing queue
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe the problem.

When using http.sys delegation, there are two processes involved, the delegator (the process creating the DelegationRule to delegate requests it receives) and the receiver (the process the delegator transfers requests to). It's possible that the receiver may restart independently from the delegator. When using the http.sys server as a receiver with the `RequestQueueMode.Create` option, the receiver fails to start up because the delegator still has a handle to the queue. If the `RequestQueueMode.CreateOrAttach` option is used, the receiver start up fine but fails to receive any traffic because there are no URL groups configured in http.sys.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Either add a new option to RequestQueueMode to indicate that URL groups should be configured when attaching or always try to create these when attaching if specified and they don't already exist.

### Additional context

_No response_
comments: Could creating the URL group cause a conflict with another process that has added the same prefixes?

For the same queue or a different one? If for a different one, doesn't that issue already exist today? I don't think http.sys will let you create a URL group if it would collide with an existing one, but I could try it out.
If you have multiple instances of the same app all running in CreateOrAttach mode with the same prefixes and queue, would they conflict with eachother if they all made the same url group?

Thanks for contacting us.

We're moving this issue to the `.NET 7 Planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. We would like to keep this around to collect more feedback, which can help us with prioritizing this work. We will re-evaluate this issue, during our next planning meeting(s). 
If we later determine, that the issue has no community involvement, or it's very rare and low-impact issue, we will close it - so that the team can focus on more important and high impact issues.
To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/TriageProcess.md).

Yes, but clarification on terminology, creating the URL group would be fine since you don't specify any URL prefixes during creation, you just create a new one which links it to the server's session. 

It's later on when you try to add a URL prefix to the previously created URL group that you get the error `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS`.

Specifically here:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ffb8eb2cce47016b9436df1cf796968cf6caddf5/src/Servers/HttpSys/src/NativeInterop/UrlGroup.cs#L116-L123

One odd thing is if you start the second server with a different URL prefix, with some changes I made locally, it will attach to the queue, create a new session, a new URL group, and register the new prefix with its URL group. The odd part is if you make a request to the new URL, the first server actually receives the request. I didn't expect that. I'll ask the http.sys team about it.

I checked back in with the http.sys team and their suggestion was to just aways try to create the URL prefixes when attaching and handle the error (or call HttpFindUrlGroupId before trying to create). 

I'm thinking one option would be to try and create the URL prefixes if one was explicitly specified? The other option would be to add another mode `CreateOrAttachAndCreateUrlPrefix` (or something like that). 

As for the odd behavior I saw with two servers attached to the same queue with different prefixes. They actually do both end up serving traffic to either URL prefix.

Per our chat, we will change to the following behavior:

- When CreateOrAttach mode is used
- If we end up attaching and one or more URL prefixes are actually specified (vs using fallback first available)
- We will query to see if the URL prefixes are registered
- If they are not registered, we will register them

review_comments: I made this change because it made the code a bit cleaner IMO and makes more logical sense to me. I get that this may make it harder to back port changes though so if this is undesirable, it was the last commit so I can easily revert it.
